case.evidence_kind: stipulated finite model, not measured physics

facts.text: Two initially aligned panels must retain at least 4 units at ticks 3–6, then separate with all installed retainers removed by boundary 10. No damage/discard/substitution/outside resource.
One operator; one action per integer tick, completes next boundary. Resources cannot occupy two places simultaneously. H initially intact; all other parts free.
detach(H) frees M and S; assemble(H) requires both free. Neither creates retention. H requires M and S to remain assembled for tap.
tap(P1/P2) requires intact H and free pin; each installed pin supplies 2 units. pull removes installed pin. Only pins add capacities; no pins with non-pin retainer.
install(C) supplies 4 retention; remove(C) removes clip.
install(V) then insert(S,V) with detached/free S supplies min(4,4) retention; withdraw(S,V) then remove(V) releases.
place(M) after detach(H), then route(L), supplies min(2,4) retention. unroute(L) then lift(M) releases. Both are needed.
install(Q) supplies theta in {0,4}; theta is initially unmeasured. measure(Q) returns exact theta in one tick, never itself creates retention. remove(Q) releases. No assumed theta.
At most one non-pin retaining assembly installed; it cannot combine with pins. No unlisted operation, adhesive, welding, elastic extrapolation or sustained manual support.
The conventional archive contains two-pin fastening and clip fastening. All supported properties are common to all arms; these known constructions are not locally original.
The discrete-fastener grammar and impact budget b=2 are soft benchmark conventions/preferences, not mechanical laws. b may be set to 2,1,0 only in declared ladder cells.
Available identities: ['H', 'M', 'S', 'P1', 'P2', 'C', 'V', 'L']. Capacity values above are complete; unknowns are not free variables.

attack.failure: The deliberately wrong single-pin exercise supplies only 2 units against demand 3; it also retains H as an operating dependency. This is an instructed negative exercise, not an organic failure of CORE:S01.
attack.invariant: The initially aligned panels must retain at least 3 units throughout ticks 3–6, then release for separation with every installed retainer removed by boundary 10, without damage, discard, substitution, or outside resources.
attack.permitted_variable: Remove intact H from the operating route by detach(H), then use its freed S with available V. Neither the demand nor the release boundary changes.

budget_used.allocation: Before construction: reserve one candidate slot for the forced single-pin negative exercise and one for a sleeve-and-stem attempt after removing the H operating dependency. Leave the third candidate slot and four of six search slots unused; no fresh builder.
budget_used.limits: At most 3 constructions; this practice uses 2. Maximum 1800 normalized JSON words. Word caps are not equal compute. No outside search or additional model calls.

candidates.burden: Two operator actions occupy ticks 0 and 7. H remains intact. Low action burden cannot compensate for the missing retention unit.
candidates.defeat: At every required hold tick, the sole installed pin provides 2 units, below demand 3. This negative baseline also depends on intact H and therefore is not the method-compliant counterexample.
candidates.lineage: Initial construction deliberately requested as a negative exercise. Constructed before the method-compliant attempt; never selected as a working route and not counted as spontaneous discovery or organic method failure.
candidates.mechanism: Intact H installs P1 at boundary 1. One pin contributes exactly 2 units until pull at tick 7 completes at boundary 8. There is no second pin and no additional retainer.
candidates.prediction: Modeled prediction for root replay: actions have the required mechanical prerequisites, but hold retention is 2 rather than 3. Release occurs by boundary 8. The archive two-pin route would supply 4; reducing it to one pin loses required function.

candidates.burden: Five operator actions occupy ticks 0, 1, 2, 7, and 8. S is committed to V during the hold, so H cannot be assembled during that interval. M remains free. Compared with conventional two-pin installation and removal, this route adds one disassembly action while eliminating tapping.
candidates.defeat: A later insert would miss the first required hold tick; early withdrawal would remove required retention; removing V before withdrawing S would violate the stipulated release sequence. Using intact H again would abandon the dependency-removal procedure.
candidates.lineage: Initial method-compliant construction following the explicitly forced negative exercise. No received outputs, feedback, historical construction, or helpers used.
candidates.mechanism: detach(H) completes at boundary 1, removing intact H and freeing S and M. install(V) completes at boundary 2. insert(S,V) completes at boundary 3 and produces min(3,3)=3 units without tapping or pins. withdraw completes at boundary 8; remove(V) completes at boundary 9. H is never reassembled or used for impact.
candidates.prediction: Modeled prediction for root replay: retention reaches 3 exactly at boundary 3 and persists through ticks 3–6. All installed retainers are removed by boundary 9, enabling separation before boundary 10. This is an explicit candidate counterexample to the necessity of intact H for the unchanged function. It uses zero taps within the default impact preference 2 and declares no ladder change. Mechanical outcome remains pending root replay; this is not measured physics or a final evaluator verdict.

handoff.residue: There is no setup slack: insertion completes exactly at the first required hold boundary. H remains split after release; restoring H is neither included nor required by J01. Disassembly uses H as a source of S, while intact H is absent from the retaining and release operations.
handoff.summary: Replay the labeled negative independently from the initial state: tap(P1) at 0, pull(P1) at 7; predict insufficient 2-unit retention, with failure deliberately induced. Replay the working attempt independently from the initial state: detach(H) at 0, install(V) at 1, insert(S,V) at 2, withdraw(S,V) at 7, remove(V) at 8. Predict 3 units at required ticks 3–6 and release by boundary 9. Preserve one operator, one action per tick, next-boundary completion, exclusive resource occupancy, no concurrent non-pin assembly or pins, and all hard requirements. Use only available identities and literal primitives. No Q or assumed theta, no outside material or sustained manual support. Evaluate predictions with the root replay; no self-assigned result.

attack.failure: Actual first-practice replay rejected the deliberately forced single-pin exercise: 2 units failed demand 3 at every hold tick. It confirmed the sleeve-and-stem sequence at demand 3. Neither result establishes performance at this demand 4. The organic boundary considered here is head-and-loop capacity: removing intact H does not make its 2-unit head sufficient.
attack.invariant: Initially aligned panels must retain at least 4 units at ticks 3–6, then separate with all installed retainers removed by boundary 10, without damage, discard, substitution, or outside resources.
attack.permitted_variable: CORE:S01 removes intact H as the operating dependency through detach(H). Available C or S with V can supply the unchanged demand; M with L remains bounded by head capacity. No tap or reassembly restores H.

candidates.burden: Five operator actions; setup consumes ticks 0–2 with no slack before hold. S occupies V during hold, preventing H assembly. M stays free. Relative to two-pin fastening this adds one action and eliminates both taps.
candidates.defeat: Insertion delayed beyond tick 2 misses the first hold boundary. Withdrawal before hold ends loses retention. Lower capacity than the stipulated 4 would defeat this route; T1 replay alone cannot rule that out in another case.
candidates.lineage: Transferred from AC16-T-practice1 actual replay: identical five-action sequence had no replay errors and held 3 at ticks 3–6. Recomputed under literal T2 stem and sleeve capacities 4, rather than assuming the former outcome transfers.
candidates.mechanism: Detach completes at boundary 1 and frees S and M. Install V completes at 2; insert S,V completes at 3 and supplies min(4,4)=4. Withdraw completes at 8; remove V completes at 9. Intact H is absent throughout retention and release.
candidates.prediction: Modeled T2 prediction: 4 units throughout required ticks and release by boundary 9 with zero impacts. This would counterexample necessity of intact H if root replay confirms all constraints. The observed feedback was a stipulated-model T1 replay, not measured physics; T2 evaluation remains pending.

candidates.burden: Three actions. Detach adds an action unnecessary to clipping mechanically, but explicitly enforces removal of the preferred operating dependency. S and M stay free; H remains split. Clip setup completes one boundary before first hold.
candidates.defeat: A clip installed after tick 2 misses hold onset; removal before hold ends loses retention. Combining C with pins or another non-pin assembly is forbidden. This known archive construction cannot establish local originality.
candidates.lineage: Second T2 construction uses the packet-defined conventional clip route and explicitly removes H. It is not inferred from a successful clip replay; first-practice feedback only supplied sleeve and single-pin results.
candidates.mechanism: Detach completes at 1. Install C completes at 2 and directly supplies 4 without impacts or use of H parts. Remove C completes at 8, leaving no installed retainer.
candidates.prediction: Modeled prediction: 4 units at ticks 3–6, release by boundary 8, zero taps. It provides a second candidate counterexample to H necessity with two fewer actions than sleeve engagement. Mechanical feasibility awaits root replay; archive membership limits novelty.

candidates.burden: Five actions and no setup slack. M is committed during hold and cannot assemble H; S remains free. Extra loop capacity cannot relieve the head bottleneck. Release needs both unroute and lift.
candidates.defeat: min(head 2, loop 4)=2 is below unchanged demand 4 at every required hold tick. Adding pins or another non-pin assembly to rescue this construction violates J09. No admissible timing change raises capacity.
candidates.lineage: Third T2 construction applies the same named procedure to freed M and available L. This is an organic insufficiency boundary of that route, not the instructed T1 single-pin negative exercise and not a failure of all dependency-removal routes.
candidates.mechanism: Detach completes at 1, place M at 2, and route L at 3. Both required parts are engaged, but retention is only min(2,4)=2. Unroute at 7 and lift at 8 finish release by boundary 9.
candidates.prediction: Modeled prediction: valid timing and removal sequence, but insufficient retention 2 versus 4 throughout hold. Root must replay this honest expected failure independently. It cannot establish H necessity because other candidate routes supply stipulated capacity 4.

handoff.residue: Sleeve and loop setup finish exactly at boundary 3. Every attempt leaves H split; restoring it is not required by J01. Clip disassembly is an explicit procedural burden. The head-and-loop failure is anticipated from complete capacities, not an evaluator result or an invented physical observation.
handoff.summary: Replay each candidate independently from the initial state using its exact tick/op/arg actions. Same CORE:S01 in all three: detach H and never assemble or tap. Keep demand 4, hold ticks 3–6, removal boundary 10, one operator and next-boundary completion. Only one non-pin assembly, no pins alongside it, no outside resources. Sleeve predicts 4 and release at 9; clip predicts 4 and release at 8; head-loop predicts only 2 and release at 9. First-practice replay confirmed sleeve at demand 3 and rejected a forced single-pin negative. T2 results are pending. Q is unavailable and theta unmeasured; do not assume it. No impact ladder change or novelty claim for the known clip route.
